name: tstmd-contraction-reorientation
title: Cell contraction & fiber reorientation (real TST-MD, 2D)
question: In the real 2D static-adhesion hybrid CPM + bead-spring ECM engine (Tsingos et al. 2023, the published ancestor of Merks' 3D model), does a contractile cell contract against a crosslinked ECM and reorient the surrounding fibers toward itself, reproducing the direction of the 3D paper's remodeling result?
hypothesis: A contractile cell coupled to the fiber network via static adhesions will contract over Monte Carlo time and drag/align nearby fibers toward it, so the fraction of radially-aligned fibers (q) rises above its initial value (q/q0 > 1), as in Keijzer & Merks 2026 Fig 4.
objective: Run one seeded coupled simulation (single contractile cell, 1200 fiber strands, ~3750 crosslinks, 300 MCS) through the real engine and measure the cell-area and reorientation (q/q0) trajectories plus start/end snapshots.
description: REAL output of the TST-MD engine, driven CPU-only via the viva-tstmd Docker bridge (TST C++ + HOOMD + MUSCLE3). Single contractile cell (size_init_cells=120, target_area=10, lambda=50) in a crosslinked bead-spring ECM. q = fraction of fibers with alignment gamma>=0.9 to the cell centroid (paper eq. 7); q0 is the initial value. This is a 2D, mechanism-level analog of Keijzer & Merks 2026 (arXiv:2609.02375) Fig 4 reorientation — not a quantitative figure match (see investigation caveats).
claim: The real engine reproduces, in 2D, the direction of the 3D paper's mechanical-reciprocity result: a contractile cell contracts (13135 -> ~10 lattice sites over ~80 MCS) and reorients fibers toward itself (q/q0 rises 1.00 -> ~1.09 and holds).
expected_behavior: Cell area decreases monotonically from its initial value as the cell contracts
Fiber reorientation q/q0 rises above 1.0 and stays above 1.0 (fibers align toward the cell)

readouts.name: Cell area
readouts.description: Count of lattice sites with spin sigma>=1 (the contractile cell), per state dump.

readouts.name: Reorientation ratio
readouts.description: Fraction of fibers nearly radial to the cell (gamma>=0.9, paper eq. 7) normalised by the initial value; q/q0>1 means fibers reorient toward the cell.

behavior_tests.name: Contractile cell contracts against the ECM
behavior_tests.description: The cell area falls to below 10% of its initial value over the run. Measured from the real run: 13135 -> 10 lattice sites (>99% reduction) by MCS ~80.
behavior_tests.paper_reference: Keijzer & Merks 2026, Fig 2/3 (contraction of a contractile cell in ECM)

behavior_tests.name: Fibers reorient toward the contracting cell (q/q0 > 1)
behavior_tests.description: Peak and final q/q0 exceed 1.05, i.e. the contracting cell measurably aligns nearby fibers toward itself. Measured: q/q0 1.00 -> peak ~1.10, final ~1.09.
behavior_tests.paper_reference: Keijzer & Merks 2026, Fig 4A-B (q/q0 > 1 reorientation toward cell)

embed_visualizations.title: Contraction dynamics + fiber reorientation (+ start/end ECM snapshots)

evidence.from_test: Contractile cell contracts against the ECM

findings.statement: The real TST-MD engine reproduces the DIRECTION of the 3D paper's remodeling result in 2D: a contractile cell contracts against the crosslinked ECM (13135 -> ~10 lattice sites) and reorients fibers toward itself (q/q0 1.00 -> ~1.09).

At this parameter regime the cell's equilibrium area is set by its target area (10), not by ECM resistance — so this study demonstrates the contraction + reorientation MECHANISM, not the quantitative ECM-limited-equilibrium relationship of Fig 2. Closing that gap requires model calibration (physical->ymmsl unit scaling); documented as the investigation's open calibration item.

conclusion: Using the real published engine, a 2D contractile cell contracts against a crosslinked bead-spring ECM and reorients nearby fibers toward itself (q/q0>1), reproducing the direction of Keijzer & Merks 2026's Fig 4. The magnitude/equilibrium relationship (Fig 2) is a documented calibration gap, not claimed here.
key_assumptions: 2D (the real engine is 2D; the target paper is 3D) — mechanism/direction analog only.
Static adhesions (as in the 3D paper), not the dynamic focal adhesions of Keijzer et al. 2025.
Reduced size vs the paper's HPC scale (1200 strands, 300 MCS) for CPU tractability.
1 seed; q uses the gamma>=0.9 radial-alignment threshold of paper eq. 7.
